claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Vogg et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Labeling experiments have demonstrated that pattern formation in Hydra re-aggregates arises de novo and that cells sort themselves only in regards to their germ layer identity.
claims.source: Labeling experiments have demonstrated that pattern formation in re-aggregates arises de novo and that cells sort themselves only in regards to their germ layer identity (Technau and Holstein, 1992; Technau et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Technau and Holstein, 1992; Technau et al., 2000.

claims.claim: Oral halves of Nematostella mid-gastrulae, which contain a population of blastopore lip cells with axial organizer capability conveyed by Wnt1 and Wnt3, were able to reorganize the body plan and develop into a functional polyp.
claims.source: Oral halves, which contain a population of blastopore lip cells with axial organizer capability conveyed by Wnt1 and Wnt3, were able to reorganize the body plan and develop into a functional polyp.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from a study on Nematostella reaggregation (Kirillova et al., 2018).

claims.claim: Aboral halves of Nematostella mid-gastrulae were only capable of reconstituting an animal upon prior injection of both Wnts.
claims.source: Accordingly, aboral halves were only capable of reconstituting an animal upon prior injection of both Wnts, demonstrating that a competent cell population (ESC-LPs) is needed for generation of a re-aggregate capable of developing into a functional animal.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from a study on Nematostella reaggregation (Kirillova et al., 2018).

claims.claim: A competent cell population (ESC-LPs) is needed for generation of a Nematostella re-aggregate capable of developing into a functional animal.
claims.source: Accordingly, aboral halves were only capable of reconstituting an animal upon prior injection of both Wnts, demonstrating that a competent cell population (ESC-LPs) is needed for generation of a re-aggregate capable of developing into a functional animal.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental data on Nematostella reaggregation.

claims.claim: A stem cell population in a more naïve state, from embryos prior to the gastrula stage, should harbor the full developmental potential to self-organize the body axes without external inputs.
claims.source: Therefore, a stem cell population in a more naïve state, from embryos prior to the gastrula stage, should, in theory, harbor the full developmental potential to self-organize the body axes without external inputs.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference based on observations from Nematostella reaggregation experiments.

claims.claim: Cells in developing embryonic Nematostella re-aggregates exhibit vast reprogramming of their axial identity.
claims.source: Akin to corresponding experiments in adult Hydra, cells in developing embryonic Nematostella re-aggregates exhibit vast reprogramming of their axial identity.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from Nematostella reaggregation studies.

claims.claim: In Nematostella re-aggregates, ectodermal cells could convert into endoderm, but endodermal cells remained endodermal.
claims.source: Notably, while ectodermal cells could convert into endoderm, the latter remained endodermal.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from Nematostella reaggregation studies.

claims.claim: In case Nematostella re-aggregates were generated purely from endoderm, cells became mesenchymal and migratory causing aggregates to collapse.
claims.source: However, in case re-aggregates were generated purely from endoderm, cells became mesenchymal and migratory causing aggregates to collapse.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from Nematostella reaggregation studies.

claims.claim: Nematostella re-aggregates which successfully reform a functional animal employ a developmental mode distinct to normal Nematostella embryogenesis, but similar to other cnidarians, such as hydrozoans.
claims.source: Perhaps, most intriguing though is the observation that re-aggregates which successfully reform a functional animal employ a developmental mode distinct to normal Nematostella embryogenesis, but similar to other cnidarians, such as hydrozoans.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on observations from Nematostella reaggregation studies.

claims.claim: In Nematostella re-aggregates, germ layer specification occurs via delamination of the ectoderm, ingression of endodermal plate cells, and cavitation of inner cells, instead of invagination.
claims.source: Namely, instead of invagination, germ layer specification occurs via delamination of the ectoderm, ingression of those endodermal plate cells that were initially located at the aggregate surface due to random mixing, as well as cavitation of inner cells.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from Nematostella reaggregation studies.

claims.claim: Cell aggregates obtained by dissociating chordamesoderm from the early Xenopus gastrula undergo cell sorting and convergent extension to establish an anteroposterior patterning in an elongated structure revealed through the expression of Bra/T (Xbra) and Chordin.
claims.source: In Xenopus, cell aggregates obtained by dissociating chordamesoderm (prospective notochord) from the early gastrula were shown to undergo cell sorting and convergent extension to establish an anteroposterior patterning in an elongated structure revealed through the expression of Bra/T (Xbra) and Chordin (Ninomiya et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ninomiya et al., 2004.

claims.claim: By addition of Activin A to dissociated Xenopus animal cap cells, they were shown to generate multiple mesodermal tissue types.
claims.source: By addition of Activin A to these cells, they were shown to generate multiple mesodermal tissue types (Green and Smith, 1990) and, depending on the dosage of the signal, these consist almost entirely of notochord (Green et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Green and Smith, 1990 and Green et al., 1992.

claims.claim: Depending on the dosage of Activin A, dissociated Xenopus animal cap cells can consist almost entirely of notochord.
claims.source: By addition of Activin A to these cells, they were shown to generate multiple mesodermal tissue types (Green and Smith, 1990) and, depending on the dosage of the signal, these consist almost entirely of notochord (Green et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Green et al., 1992.

claims.claim: When dissociated Xenopus animal cap cells are allowed to re-aggregate spontaneously, they round up into a ball followed by elongation and organization of an axis in a manner whereby the axial extrusion resembles archenteron elongation in deuterostomes.
claims.source: Perhaps, even more remarkable is the scenario when such dissociated cells are allowed to re-aggregate spontaneously: They round up into a ball followed by elongation and organization of an axis in a manner whereby the axial extrusion resembles archenteron elongation in deuterostomes, for instance sea urchins (Green et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Green et al., 2004.

claims.claim: Isolated blastoderms of Fundulus heteroclitus, deprived of yolk, can develop into embryo-like structures.
claims.source: It was shown that isolated blastoderms of Fundulus heteroclitus, deprived of yolk, can develop into embryo-like structures (Oppenheimer, 1936).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Oppenheimer, 1936.

claims.claim: Uncommitted embryonic cells of animal caps in 128-cell stage zebrafish embryos were shown to organize a complete embryonic axis upon injection of opposing gradients of BMP and Nodal.
claims.source: Furthermore, uncommitted embryonic cells of animal caps in 128-cell stage zebrafish embryos were shown to organize a complete embryonic axis upon injection of opposing gradients of BMP and Nodal (Xu et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Pescoids, when allowed to grow without the supply of external signals, were shown to be robust to cell mixing and able to form a polarized domain of high Bra/T (tbxta) expression, leading to further elongation under the influence of Nodal and non-canonical Wnt (PCP) signaling.
claims.source: These ex vivo systems, when allowed to grow without the supply of external signals, were shown to be robust to cell mixing, able to form a polarized domain of high Bra/T (tbxta) expression, leading to further elongation under the influence of Nodal (similar to amphibian requirement for Activin) and non-canonical Wnt (PCP) signaling.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from pescoid studies.

claims.claim: Pescoids specify all germ layers and most mesodermal lineage precursors in terms of marker gene expression.
claims.source: In addition, they specify all germ layers and most mesodermal lineage precursors in terms of marker gene expression (Fulton et al., 2020; Schauer et al., 2020; Williams and Solnica-Krezel, 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fulton et al., 2020; Schauer et al., 2020; Williams and Solnica-Krezel, 2020.

claims.claim: Explant systems have been derived from the Mexican tetra Astyanax mexicanus.
claims.source: Lately, such explant system have also been derived from the Mexican tetra Astyanax mexicanus (Torres-Paz and Retaux, 2021) and the Japanese rice fish or medaka Oryzias latipes (Zilova et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Torres-Paz and Retaux, 2021.

claims.claim: In medaka, blastoderm cells were re-aggregated and exposed to factors which facilitate neural development to generate anterior structures recapitulating retinal differentiation as well as morphogenesis.
claims.source: In the latter case, blastoderm cells were re-aggregated and exposed to factors which facilitate neural development to generate anterior structures recapitulating retinal differentiation as well as morphogenesis.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from medaka explant studies (Zilova et al., 2021).

claims.claim: Pescoids require polarized inheritance of maternal factors.
claims.source: Results in amniotic embryos need to be interpreted with care since the embryonic cells inherit maternal signals starting at the single cell stage, as it was indeed shown for pescoids that require polarized inheritance of maternal factors (Schauer et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Schauer et al., 2020.

claims.claim: In annual killifish, complete dispersion of pre-embryonic blastomeres is followed by their re-aggregation to generate embryonic body plan.
claims.source: In their natural settings, the phenomenon of complete dispersion of pre-embryonic blastomeres in annual killifish (Austrofundulus myersi Wourms, 1972, Austrolebias charrua Pereiro et al., 2017), followed by their re-aggregation to generate embryonic body plan is the closest observation to complete dissociation of teleost cells.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Wourms, 1972 and Pereiro et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Annual killifish represent an exceptional in vivo testimony to the notion of multiple developmental trajectories being available to the embryonic cells as seen in the differential rate of specification of anterior and posterior structures in embryos that have and have not undergone diapause.
claims.source: While it is not clear to what extent the organization of dissociated cells is autonomous and independent of extraembryomic cues, annual killifish, intriguingly, represent an exceptional in vivo testimony to the notion of multiple developmental trajectories being available to the embryonic cells as seen in the differential rate of specification of anterior and posterior structures in embryos that have and have not undergone diapause (Podrabsky et al., 2010; Romney et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Podrabsky et al., 2010; Romney et al., 2018.

claims.claim: 3D aggregates termed embryoid bodies can give rise to progenitor cells for the germ layers as well as form rudiments of tissues and organs without the context of an embryo.
claims.source: Pioneering work on 3D aggregates, termed embryoid bodies (EBs), has demonstrated that these can give rise to progenitor cells for the germ layers as well as form rudiments of tissues and organs without the context of an embryo (Doetschman et al., 1985; Desbaillets et al., 2000; Brickman and Serup, 2017).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Doetschman et al., 1985; Desbaillets et al., 2000; Brickman and Serup, 2017.

claims.claim: Polarized gene expression and self-organized axial emergence in embryoid bodies has been shown to be mediated by Wnt signaling.
claims.source: Polarized gene expression and self-organized axial emergence in embryoid bodies has been shown to be mediated by Wnt signaling (ten Berge et al., 2008; Sagy et al., 2019), although the extent of displayed axial organization is limited.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to ten Berge et al., 2008; Sagy et al., 2019.

claims.claim: mGastruloids mimic some morphogenetic events of early mouse embryos, such as elongation, germ layer as well as axis formation and associated patterning.
claims.source: mGastruloids are initially spherical aggregates derived from few hundreds of homogenous mESCs which, although removed from extraembryonic tissues and nearly all associated signaling and mechanical cues, mimic some morphogenetic events of early mouse embryos, such as elongation, germ layer as well as axis formation and associated patterning (van den Brink et al., 2014; Beccari et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to van den Brink et al., 2014; Beccari et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Under differentiation conditions, mouse embryo P19 carcinoma cells are able to form polarized, elongated structures.
claims.source: Initially mGastruloids were developed motivated by the observation that, under differentiation conditions, mouse embryo P19 carcinoma cells are able to form polarized, elongated structures (Marikawa et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Marikawa et al., 2009.

claims.claim: Gastruloids have been extrapolated to hESCs (hGastruloids).
claims.source: Lately, they have also been extrapolated to hESCs (hGastruloids) (Moris et al., 2020a; Marikawa et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Moris et al., 2020a; Marikawa et al., 2020.

claims.claim: AP axis specification in mGastruloid aggregates is demarcated by autonomous polarization of previously homogeneously distributed canonical Wnt and Bra/T expression, constituting the first system-wide symmetry breaking event identified thus far.
claims.source: AP axis specification in aggregates is demarcated by autonomous polarization of previously homogeneously distributed canonical Wnt and Bra/T expression, constituting the first system-wide symmetry breaking event identified thus far (Turner et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Turner et al., 2017.

claims.claim: After 6–7 days in non-adherent culture, mGastruloids develop transcriptionally demarcated AP, DV, and ML axes, and display spatiotemporal expression of hox gene clusters similar to those in mouse at roughly embryonic day (E) 9.0–9.5.
claims.source: After 6–7 days in non-adherent culture, mGastruloids not only develop transcriptionally demarcated AP, DV, and ML axes, but also display spatiotemporal expression of hox gene clusters similar to those in mouse at roughly embryonic day (E) 9.0–9.5 (Beccari et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Beccari et al., 2018.

claims.claim: hGastruloids are generated from few hundreds of hESCs, pre-treated with a WNT agonist for 24 hr in 2D culture, then aggregated in low adherence, differentiation conditions with ongoing WNT upregulation that is subsequently diluted.
claims.source: Morphologically resembling their mouse counterpart, they are generated from few hundreds of hESCs, pre-treated with a WNT agonist for 24 hr in 2D culture, then aggregated in low adherence, differentiation conditions with ongoing WNT upregulation that is subsequently diluted.
claims.evidence: This is a description of the protocol for generating hGastruloids from the cited study.

claims.claim: In hGastruloids, BRA/T develops polarized expression a day after aggregation, thereby demarcating the posterior pole which subsequently elongates.
claims.source: BRA/T develops polarized expression a day after aggregation, thereby demarcating the posterior pole which subsequently elongates.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from hGastruloid studies.

claims.claim: After 3–4 days of development, hGastruloids reach maximal elongation and exhibit expression of genes associated with all three germ layers as well as a plethora of AP axial patterning genes, spatially organized in a manner similar to mammalian embryos.
claims.source: Already after 3–4 days of development, hGastruloids reach maximal elongation and exhibit expression of genes associated with all three germ layers as well as a plethora of AP axial patterning genes, spatially organized in a manner similar to mammalian embryos.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from hGastruloid studies.

claims.claim: In terms of their transcriptional profile, hGastruloids partly correspond to CS9 human embryos.
claims.source: Hence, in terms of their transcriptional profile, hGastruloids partly correspond to CS9 human embryos.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on transcriptional comparison of hGastruloids to human embryos.

claims.claim: For the most part, hGastruloids do not seem to recapitulate early human-specific embryonic morphology.
claims.source: Akin to mGastruloids, for the most part, they do not seem to recapitulate early human-specific embryonic morphology.
claims.evidence: This is an observation based on comparison of hGastruloids to human embryos.

claims.claim: Cell aggregates from Nematostella, zebrafish, Xenopus, mouse, and human develop an oral or posterior domain characterized by Bra/T expression in the native embryo, demarcating a symmetry-breaking event.
claims.source: Particularly with respect to the establishment of the primary axis, cell aggregates develop an oral or posterior domain characterized by Bra/T expression in the native embryo, demarcating a symmetry-breaking event (Figure 1), followed by axial elongation and AP patterning.
claims.evidence: This is a comparative observation across multiple species, with reference to Figure 1.

claims.claim: A morphological similarity – initially spherical, then elongated – can be observed between different ESC-derived systems, notwithstanding the strikingly distinct geometries of the Nematostella, fish, mouse and human embryos.
claims.source: In addition, a morphological similarity – initially spherical, then elongated – can be observed between the different systems, notwithstanding the strikingly distinct geometries of the Nematostella, fish, mouse and human embryos.
claims.evidence: This is a comparative observation across multiple ESC-derived systems.

claims.claim: Larger re-aggregates from Nematostella gastrulae form multiple oral domains.
claims.source: While the precise mechanism remains to be elucidated, another commonality is the analogous dependence of primary axis formation on the initial number of cells in aggregates from two evolutionarily highly distant species: Larger re-aggregates from Nematostella gastrulae (Kirillova et al., 2018) as well as mouse ESCs (gastruloids van den Brink et al., 2014 and embryoid bodies ten Berge et al., 2008) form multiple oral and posterior domains, respectively.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kirillova et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Larger aggregates from mouse ESCs (gastruloids and embryoid bodies) form multiple posterior domains.
claims.source: While the precise mechanism remains to be elucidated, another commonality is the analogous dependence of primary axis formation on the initial number of cells in aggregates from two evolutionarily highly distant species: Larger re-aggregates from Nematostella gastrulae (Kirillova et al., 2018) as well as mouse ESCs (gastruloids van den Brink et al., 2014 and embryoid bodies ten Berge et al., 2008) form multiple oral and posterior domains, respectively.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to van den Brink et al., 2014 and ten Berge et al., 2008.

claims.claim: Developmental similarities in ESC-derived systems reflect an inherent, converging self-organizing capability of ESCs and ESC-LPs across species when developing in the most minimal environment with the least possible external biochemical and mechanical input.
claims.source: Altogether, aforementioned developmental similarities seem to reflect an inherent, converging self-organizing capability of ESCs and ESC-LPs across species when developing in the most minimal environment with the least possible external biochemical and mechanical input.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on observed similarities across multiple ESC-derived systems.

claims.claim: This capability represents an evolutionarily conserved developmental mode which is defined as the set of developmental trajectories that cell collectives undergo as they give rise to a patterned, embryo-like structure in absence of species-specific external (micro-)environments and associated cues.
claims.source: We argue that this capability represents an evolutionarily conserved developmental mode which we define as the set of developmental trajectories – in terms of morphogenesis and gene expression dynamics – that cell collectives within a given system or aggregate from ESCs undergo as they give rise to a patterned, embryo-like structure in absence of species-specific external (micro-)environments and associated cues.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative argument with a proposed definition based on inference from observations.

claims.claim: The conserved developmental mode can differ from the mode employed by the native embryo that uses a subset of (morphogenetic) trajectories available to the highly developmentally plastic embryonic cells.
claims.source: It is noteworthy that this can indeed differ from the mode employed by the native embryo that uses a subset of (morphogenetic) trajectories available to the highly developmentally plastic embryonic cells (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on observations, with reference to Figure 2.

claims.claim: In mGastruloids, cells expressing endodermal markers appear to be specified in a manner distinct to the embryo, as they arise dispersed and subsequently congregate without the requirement of an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
claims.source: In case of mGastruloids, cells expressing endodermal markers appear to be specified in a manner distinct to the embryo, as they arise dispersed and subsequently congregate without the requirement of an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Vianello and Lutolf, 2020; Hashmi et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Vianello and Lutolf, 2020; Hashmi et al., 2020.

claims.claim: While the emerging mesendodermal lineages in early mGastruloids are similar to their in vivo equivalents, AP axis and concomitant germ layer specification occurs in a parallel, but distinct manner, initiated by a more mesenchymal-like primed ESC population as opposed to the epithelial epiblast cells of the native embryo.
claims.source: Moreover, it was recently shown, through a transcriptional comparison of early mGastruloids to the mouse embryo, that while the emerging mesendodermal lineages in vitro are similar to their in vivo equivalents, AP axis and concomitant germ layer specification occurs in a parallel, but distinct manner, initiated by a more mesenchymal-like primed ESC population as opposed to the epithelial epiblast cells of the native embryo (Anlas et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Anlas et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Cells on a separate, advanced differentiation path can be coaxed to follow basal developmental trajectories when presented with the right factors.
claims.source: Complementary to the idea of ESC(-LP)s unraveling a conserved developmental mode under minimal culture conditions, is the observation that cells on a separate, advanced differentiation path can be coaxed to follow such basal trajectories when presented with the right factors.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on observations from multiple systems.

claims.claim: In gastruloids from induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines, AP patterning dynamics, including initial Bra/T polarization, are similar to their ESC counterparts.
claims.source: Conversely, in gastruloids from induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines, AP patterning dynamics, including initial Bra/T polarization, are similar to their ESC counterparts (Beccari et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Beccari et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Single mESCs and TSCs, when grown together in a 3D Matrigel scaffold, mutually cooperate to assemble into structures (ETS embryos) highly reminiscent of the actual mouse embryo from E5.0 to 6.5.
claims.source: Single mESCs and TSCs, when grown together in a 3D Matrigel scaffold, mutually cooperate to assemble into structures, termed ETS embryos, highly reminiscent of the actual mouse embryo from E5.0 to 6.5 (Harrison et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Harrison et al., 2017.

claims.claim: ETS embryos recapitulate epiblast and trophoblast lumenogenesis, pro-amniotic cavity formation as well as mesoderm and primordial germ cell (PGC) induction.
claims.source: They recapitulate epiblast and trophoblast lumenogenesis, pro-amniotic cavity formation as well as mesoderm and primordial germ cell (PGC) induction.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from ETS embryo studies.

claims.claim: In ETS embryos, the presence of TSCs spatially confines the emergence of the Bra/T domain at the boundary between embryonic and extraembryonic compartments, akin to the natural embryo.
claims.source: Whereas in gastruloids the developing Bra/T pole or posterior seems to have no directional preference in the spherical aggregate, in ETS embryos, on the other hand, the presence of TSCs spatially confines the emergence of the this Bra/T domain at the boundary between embryonic and extraembryonic compartments, akin to the natural embryo.
claims.evidence: This is a comparative observation between gastruloids and ETS embryos.

claims.claim: The role of extraembryonic tissues in ETS embryos is in congruence with the in vivo situation, where they provide not only the right signaling environment but also the crucial geometric cues that confer robustness to a developing embryo.
claims.source: This role of the extraembryonic tissues is in congruence with the in vivo situation, where they provide not only the right signaling environment but also the crucial geometric cues that confer robustness to a developing embryo (Arnold and Robertson, 2009; Langdon and Mullins, 2011; Christodoulou et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Arnold and Robertson, 2009; Langdon and Mullins, 2011; Christodoulou et al., 2019.

claims.claim: ETX embryos display EMT, and subsequently meso- as well as endodermal marker expression, thus mimicking mouse embryo shape and morphogenesis until E7.0–7.5.
claims.source: Moreover, resulting ETX embryos display EMT, and subsequently meso- as well as endodermal marker expression, thus mimicking mouse embryo shape and morphogenesis until E7.0–7.5.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from ETX embryo studies.

claims.claim: While ETX embryos could initiate implantation responses in mouse uteri upon transplantation, they do not progress beyond this stage at the present time.
claims.source: It must be noted that, while such ETX embryos could initiate implantation responses in mouse uteri upon transplantation, they do not progress beyond this stage at the present time.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from ETX embryo transplantation experiments.

claims.claim: Inducible ETX (iETX) embryos more faithfully recapitulate particularly anterior morphogenetic events during mouse gastrulation compared to standard ETX embryos.
claims.source: Replacing XEN cells with induced endodermal cells (transgenic mESCs featuring transient Gata4 upregulation) yields inducible ETX (iETX) embryos which more faithfully recapitulate particularly anterior morphogenetic events during mouse gastrulation (Amadei et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Amadei et al., 2021.

claims.claim: The previously employed XEN cells in ETX embryos resemble the parietal endoderm rather than primitive endoderm, whereas induced endodermal cells exhibit increased developmental potential.
claims.source: This appears to be due to the previously employed XEN cells resembling the parietal endoderm rather than primitive endoderm, whereas induced endodermal cells exhibit increased developmental potential.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about why iETX embryos perform better than standard ETX embryos.

claims.claim: iETX embryos form an anterior signaling center and display anterior visceral endoderm (AVE) migration, two hallmarks of mouse gastrulation.
claims.source: iETX embryos hence form an anterior signaling center and display anterior visceral endoderm (AVE) migration, two hallmarks of mouse gastrulation.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from iETX embryo studies.

claims.claim: Blastoids, originally made from aggregated mESCs and TSCs, form structures closely resembling mouse E3.5 blastocysts (morphologically and transcriptionally) with an outer trophoectoderm layer encapsulating the blastocoel, a fluid filled cavity, as well as the epiblast.
claims.source: Blastoids, originally made from aggregated mESCs and TSCs, illustrate how the two cell types influence each other to form structures closely resembling mouse E3.5 blastocysts (morphologically and transcriptionally) with an outer trophoectoderm layer encapsulating the blastocoel, a fluid filled cavity, as well as the epiblast (Rivron et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Rivron et al., 2018.

claims.claim: In blastoids, TSCs guide the ESCs along their native developmental trajectory, and the ESCs in turn maintain proliferation and self-renewal of TSCs as well as the trophoblast epithelial morphogenesis.
claims.source: It appears that, not only do the TSCs guide the ESCs along their native developmental trajectory, the ESCs in turn maintain proliferation and self-renewal of TSCs as well as the trophoblast epithelial morphogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the mutual interactions between TSCs and ESCs in blastoids.

claims.claim: Blastoids are capable of eliciting an implantation-like response in vivo.
claims.source: Although blastoids will not form bona fide embryos, they are capable of eliciting an implantation-like response in vivo, thereby constituting a potentially useful model system for studying mouse pre-gastrulation patterning dynamics.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from blastoid studies.

claims.claim: EPS-blastoids are generated from extended pluripotent stem cells (EPSCs) and TSCs.
claims.source: In particular, EPS-blastoids are generated from extended pluripotent stem cells (EPSCs), pluripotent SCs cultured under conditions which enable both embryonic and extraembryonic developmental potential, as well as TSCs.
claims.evidence: This is a description of how EPS-blastoids are generated.

claims.claim: EPS-blastoids generate a primitive endoderm (PE)-like layer which gives rise to cells expressing parietal endoderm markers.
claims.source: These generate a primitive endoderm (PE)-like layer which, unlike normal blastoids, gives rise to cells expressing parietal endoderm markers.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from EPS-blastoid studies.

claims.claim: Under specific culture conditions, a subset of EPS-blastoids proceed to develop a post-implantation embryo-like morphology, similar to ETX embryos and E5.0-E5.5 cultured mouse embryos.
claims.source: Moreover, under specific culture conditions, a subset of EPS-blastoids proceed to develop a post-implantation embryo-like morphology, similar to ETX embryos and E5.0-E5.5 cultured mouse embryos.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from EPS-blastoid studies.

claims.claim: The majority of advanced EPS-blastoids form an outer visceral endoderm (VE)-like layer.
claims.source: The majority of these advanced EPS-blastoids also form an outer visceral endoderm (VE)-like layer.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from EPS-blastoid studies.

claims.claim: Human blastocyst-like structures (hBlastoids) can be successfully obtained by either mixing hESCs with SCs from extra-embryonic lineages or via employing naïve hEPSCs.
claims.source: A series of very recent studies with hPSCs (induced or otherwise) demonstrated that also human blastocyst-like structures (hBlastoids) can be successfully obtained by either mixing hESCs with SCs from extra-embryonic lineages or via employing naïve hEPSCs, akin to the mouse model (Liu et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2021; Sozen et al., 2021; Fan et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2021; Sozen et al., 2021; Fan et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Application of matrigel to mGastruloids generates somite-like structures in conjunction with respective gene oscillation during mGastruloid elongation.
claims.source: For example, a recent work reports the application of matrigel to generate somite-like structutures in conjunction with respective gene oscillation during mGastruloid elongation (van den Brink et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to van den Brink et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Wnt inhibition in conjunction with matrigel embedding promotes anterior segment formation and improves physical separation of somites in mGastruloids.
claims.source: A parallel study adds that Wnt inhibition in conjunction with matrigel embedding further promotes anterior segment formation and improves physical separation of somites (Veenvliet et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Veenvliet et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Upon administration of cardiogenic factors FGF, VEGF and ascorbic acid, mGastruloids reproducibly recapitulate cardiogenesis at their anterior end, giving rise a vascular-like network, first and second heart fields as well as ultimately a beating structure, resembling an actual embryonic heart.
claims.source: Upon administration of cardiogenic factors FGF, VEGF and ascorbic acid, mGastruloids reproducibly recapitulate cardiogenesis at their anterior end, giving rise a vascular-like network, first and second heart fields as well as ultimately a beating structure, resembling an actual embryonic heart (Rossi et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Rossi et al., 2021.

claims.claim: mGastruloids generated from mESCs and XEN cells ('neuruloids') exhibit increased cell type diversity and develop neural-tube-like structures.
claims.source: Moreover, mGastruloids generated not only from mESCs but also from XEN cells ('neuruloids') exhibit increased cell type diversity and develop neural-tube-like structures (Berenger-Currias et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Berenger-Currias et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Post-implantation epiblast-like (EPI) gastruloids specify anterior neural tissues upon additional Wnt inhibition via XAV939, while still developing an elongated morphology.
claims.source: Another study details the generation of post-implantation epiblast-like (EPI) gastruloids which, in contrast to standard mGastruloids, specify anterior neural tissues upon additional Wnt inhibition via XAV939, while still developing an elongated morphology (Girgin et al., 2021b).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Girgin et al., 2021b.

claims.claim: Epi-aggregates were combined with TSC aggregates to generate structures labeled EpiTS embryoids that undergo axial elongation and concomitant patterning.
claims.source: Epi-aggregates were combined with TSC aggregates to generate structures labeled EpiTS embryoids that undergo axial elongation and concomitant patterning (Girgin et al., 2021a).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Girgin et al., 2021a.

claims.claim: Addition of matrigel to epithelialize the Epi-aggregates restricts the onset of Bra/T expression at the boundary between Epi-ESCs and TSCs, akin to the native embryo as well as the ETS/ETX embryo.
claims.source: Addition of matrigel to epithelialize the Epi-aggregates restricts the onset of Bra/T expression at the boundary between Epi-ESCs and TSCs, akin to the native embryo as well as the ETS/ETX embryo.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from EpiTS embryoid studies.

claims.claim: At later stages in EpiTS embryoids, (anterior) neural patterning is augmented whereas mesendoderm differentiation is diminished.
claims.source: At later stages (anterior) neural patterning is augmented whereas mesendoderm differentiation is diminished.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from EpiTS embryoid studies.

claims.claim: Two disparately sized ESC aggregates were fused after an initial aggregation and growth phase, with the smaller one serving as a signaling center through brief exposure to BMP4, resulting in embryo-like structures that specify the three germ layers and proceed to develop until the equivalent of mouse embryo E9.0.
claims.source: In a conceptually similar approach, two disparately sized ESC aggregates were fused after an initial aggregation and growth phase (Xu et al., 2021), with the smaller one serving as a signaling center through brief exposure to BMP4, a factor known to induce gastrulation and axis formation in mammals (Winnier et al., 1995). Resulting embryo-like structures specify the three germ layers and proceed to develop until the equivalent of mouse embryo E9.0.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Xu et al., 2021 and Winnier et al., 1995.

claims.claim: Fused ESC aggregates with a BMP4-exposed signaling center exhibit advanced morphogenesis compared to standard mGastruloids, with neural plate and tube-like structures, although these still appear to lack substantial forebrain and anterior midbrain populations.
claims.source: They further exhibit advanced morphogenesis compared to standard mGastruloids, with, for instance, neural plate and tube-like structures, although these still appear to lack substantial forebrain and anterior midbrain populations.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from fused ESC aggregate studies.

claims.claim: Pretreatment of human iPSCs with a Wnt agonist and FGF2 for 48 hr, followed by aggregation and maintenance in shaking culture, supplemented for 4 days with a growth factor cocktail (FGF2, HGF and IGF-1) yields gastruloids (EMLO) that can be grown over several weeks.
claims.source: Regarding human systems, it was recently demonstrated that pretreatment of human iPSCs with a Wnt agonist and FGF2 for 48 hr, followed by aggregation and maintenance in shaking culture, supplemented for 4 days with a growth factor cocktail (FGF2, HGF and IGF-1) yields gastruloids, termed EMLO, that can be grown over several weeks (Olmsted and Paluh, 2021).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Olmsted and Paluh, 2021.

claims.claim: EMLO gastruloids appear to be biased toward trunk mesendoderm and central as well as peripheral nervous system fates.
claims.source: Overall, these appear to be biased toward trunk mesendoderm and central as well as peripheral nervous system fates.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from EMLO gastruloid studies.

claims.claim: EMLO gastruloids display more complex morphology and neural cell type diversity when compared to standard hGastruloids, developing a primitive gut tube-like structure and innervation thereof.
claims.source: In particular, EMLO gastruloids display more complex morphology and neural cell type diversity when compared to standard hGastruloids, developing a primitive gut tube-like structure and, notably, innervation thereof.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from EMLO gastruloid studies.

claims.claim: By employing a microfluidic device, researchers were able to recapitulate post-implantation embryo development prior to and during early gastrulation, encompassing epiblast luminogenesis, formation of the bipolar embryonic sac and PGC as well as primitive streak cell specification.
claims.source: By employing a microfluidic device, researchers were able to recapitulate post-implantation embryo development prior to and during early gastrulation, encompassing epiblast luminogenesis, formation of the bipolar embryonic sac and PGC as well as primitive streak cell specification (Zheng et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zheng et al., 2019.

claims.claim: In amniotic-sac-like embryoids, dorsal amniotic ectoderm-like cells were induced via localized application of BMP4.
claims.source: Following lumenogenesis, dorsal amniotic ectoderm-like cells were induced via localized application of BMP4.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from amniotic-sac-like embryoid studies.

claims.claim: In amniotic-sac-like embryoids, ventral epiblast-like cells give rise to subpopulations expressing primitive streak markers such as BRA/T and PGC-associated genes.
claims.source: Ventral epiblast-like cells give rise to subpopulations expressing primitive streak markers such as BRA/T and PGC-associated genes.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from amniotic-sac-like embryoid studies.

claims.claim: After 2–3 days in culture, amniotic-sac-like embryoid cysts collapse due to emigration of ventral cells.
claims.source: After 2–3 days in culture, cysts collapse due to emigration of ventral cells.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on data from amniotic-sac-like embryoid studies.

claims.claim: Comparison of in vitro and ex vivo systems to their in vivo counterparts may point toward an underlying developmental morphospace spanning a plethora of available trajectories.
claims.source: In conjunction with the observed diversity in (pre-) gastrulation embryo shapes, comparison of in vitro and ex vivo systems to their in vivo counterparts may point toward an underlying developmental morphospace spanning a plethora of available trajectories (Mitteroecker and Huttegger, 2009).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference with a supporting citation.

claims.claim: Since embryos of a given species generally develop under the same specific inputs, including geometry and extraembryonic environment, ESCs are developmentally biased and alternative trajectories are revealed only when cells are removed from their native context and challenged by different external conditions.
claims.source: Since embryos of a given species generally develop under the same specific inputs, including geometry and extraembryonic environment, ESCs are developmentally biased and such alternative trajectories are revealed only when cells are removed from their native context and challenged by different external conditions (Figure 3).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about developmental bias, with reference to Figure 3.

claims.claim: ESC populations appear to possess an inherent capability to at least form a primary axis through a conserved developmental mode, which surfaces when ESC(-LP)s are grown in the most minimal conditions.
claims.source: Furthermore, as illustrated above, ESC populations appear to possess an inherent capability to at least form a primary axis through a conserved developmental mode, which surfaces when ESC(-LP)s are grown in the most minimal conditions.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on observations from multiple ESC-derived systems.

claims.claim: While blastoids and ETS/ETX embryos (mostly) faithfully recapitulate embryo geometry and morphogenesis, they are, at the present time, not able to develop beyond the in vivo equivalent of embryonic stage E7.0-E7.5.
claims.source: When comparing systems such as gastruloids with blastoids and ETS/ETX embryos, it becomes apparent that, while the latter (mostly) faithfully recapitulate embryo geometry and morphogenesis, they are, at the present time, not able to develop beyond the in vivo equivalent of embryonic stage E7.0-E7.5.
claims.evidence: This is a comparative observation about the developmental potential of different systems.

claims.claim: Gastruloids do not look like actual embryos and undergo a more abstracted morphogenesis, yet they are capable of reaching the partial (transcriptional) equivalent of E9.0.
claims.source: On the other hand, gastruloids do not look like actual embryos and undergo a more abstracted morphogenesis, yet they are capable of reaching the partial (transcriptional) equivalent of E9.0 (in case of the mESC-based system).
claims.evidence: This is a comparative observation about gastruloids.

claims.claim: By employing additional extraembryonic cell types or mimicking a set of in vivo cues, resulting embryo-shaped artificial systems remain more constrained in their developmental potential because they would require further precise, spatially and temporally allocated inputs to facilitate successive patterning events.
claims.source: It seems that by employing additional extraembryonic cell types or, in general terms, by mimicking a set of in vivo cues, resulting embryo-shaped artificial systems remain more constrained in their developmental potential. This is likely because, once having assumed an embryo-like developmental mode early during their respective morphogenesis, such structures would require further precise, spatially and temporally allocated inputs, just like the in vivo counterpart, in order to facilitate successive patterning events.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference about why embryo-shaped systems are more constrained.

claims.claim: Gastruloid-like aggregates from pure ESCs or ESC-LPs might represent a more unconstrained system, which is what enables them to develop beyond the equivalent of initial gastrulation, and therefore unveil the extent of inherent self-organizational capabilities of the source cells.
claims.source: Gastruloid-like aggregates from pure ESCs or ESC-LPs, on the other hand, might represent a more unconstrained system, which is what enables them to develop beyond the equivalent of initial gastrulation, and therefore unveil the extent of inherent self-organizational capabilities of the source cells.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference about why gastruloids can develop further.

claims.claim: The wide range of trajectories displayed by ESCs and ESC-LPs in vitro converge onto a conserved developmental mode under minimal conditions and collapse partly onto their native trajectories when provided with external inputs to recapitulate species-specific external environments.
claims.source: In summary, the wide range of trajectories displayed by ESCs and ESC-LPs in vitro converge onto an aforementioned conserved developmental mode under minimal conditions and collapse partly onto their native trajectories (at least for the mammalian systems) when provided with external inputs to recapitulate species-specific external environments (mechanical and chemical), facilitating increased morphological resemblance to the native embryo.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference about developmental trajectories in vitro.

claims.claim: Characterizing the fundamental conserved developmental mode may provide insights into the origin and evolution of animal body plans as well as how the complexity of animal shapes during peri-gastrulation development may have arisen via distinct extraembryonic factors.
claims.source: Characterizing this fundamental mode may perhaps ultimately provide insights into the origin and evolution of animal body plans as well as how the complexity of animal shapes during peri-gastrulation development may have arisen via distinct extraembryonic factors.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential insights from characterizing the conserved mode.

claims.claim: More phylum coverage is required to properly address the conserved developmental mode from a comprehensive evolutionarily perspective, dictating the need for novel minimal in vitro embryo-like systems from diploblasts and protostomes.
claims.source: In order to properly address this from a comprehensive evolutionarily perspective, however, more phylum coverage is required, dictating the need for novel minimal in vitro embryo-like systems from, for instance, diploblasts and protostomes.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the need for more research to test the hypothesis.

claims.claim: Refinement of a species-specific developmental mode as well as corresponding (extra-)embryonic morphology over the course of evolution ensures robustness (or canalization).
claims.source: Concerning the significance of extraembryonic environments, it could be argued that, from the multitude of ways that pre-gastrulating embryos have at their disposal to establish their initial body plan, refinement of a species-specific developmental mode as well as corresponding (extra-)embryonic morphology over the course of evolution ensures robustness (or canalization) (Siegal and Bergman, 2002; Félix and Wagner, 2008; Wagner, 2008; Melzer and Theißen, 2016): Those developmental trajectories that worked most robustly in the specific ecological and reproductive niches were further specified to maximize fitness (Kalinka and Tomancak, 2012).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis with supporting citations.

claims.claim: Diversification of insect egg size and shape are driven by shifts in the respective oviposition microenvironments.
claims.source: While this hypothesis remains unverified in metazoan embryos at large, a recent study finds that diversification of insect egg size and shape, traits which vary greatly across species, are driven by shifts in the respective oviposition microenvironments, that is, where the eggs are laid (Church et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Church et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Coordinated adherence of the insect blastoderm to the vitelline envelope influences tissue movement dynamics during gastrulation.
claims.source: Likewise, it was functionally demonstrated that coordinated adherence of the insect blastoderm to the vitelline envelope, a structure or shell surrounding the developing embryo, influences tissue movement dynamics during gastrulation (Münster et al., 2019), further highlighting the importance of morphology and embryonic-extraembryonic interactions in early patterning processes.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Münster et al., 2019.

claims.claim: External or extraembryonic environments and their complexity vary greatly across species and constitute a substantial challenge to replicate in vitro.
claims.source: Such external or extraembryonic environments and their complexity vary greatly across species and constitute a substantial challenge to replicate in vitro.
claims.evidence: This is a statement based on knowledge about the challenges of in vitro systems.

claims.claim: The complexity of extraembryonic environments could be one of the reasons why it is more straightforward to generate a functional Nematostella or Starfish larva as opposed to a fish, mouse, or human from isolated ESC-like cells.
claims.source: It is natural to speculate that this could be one of the reasons why it is more straightforward to generate a functional Nematostella or Starfish larva as opposed to a fish, mouse, or human from isolated ESC-like cells.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference about the difficulty of generating different organisms from ESC-like cells.

claims.claim: Comparing different kinds of embryo-like structures should provide tangible clues as to which aspects of embryonic development are inherent to ESCs and which parts strictly require extraembryonic input.
claims.source: Nonetheless, comparing these different kinds of embryo-like structures should therefore provide tangible clues as to which aspects of embryonic development or, more precisely, axis formation and associated morphogenesis are inherent to ESCs and which parts strictly require extraembryonic input.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about the utility of comparing embryo-like structures.

claims.claim: The developmental hourglass model delineates a phylotypic period at mid-embryogenesis during which common anatomical features (the basic body plan) for each respective phylum are established.
claims.source: The developmental hourglass model delineates a phylotypic period at mid-embryogenesis during which common anatomical features (the basic body plan) for each respective phylum are established (Duboule, 1994; Raff, 1996).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Duboule, 1994; Raff, 1996.

claims.claim: The phylotypic period is developmentally preceded and followed by phases of increased morphological and transcriptional divergence, thereby shaping a developmental 'hourglass'.
claims.source: In turn, this period is developmentally preceded and followed by phases of increased morphological and transcriptional divergence, thereby shaping a developmental 'hourglass' (Kalinka and Tomancak, 2012; Kalinka et al., 2010; Irie and Kuratani, 2014).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Kalinka and Tomancak, 2012; Kalinka et al., 2010; Irie and Kuratani, 2014.

claims.claim: 'Mid-developmental transition' (MDT) refers to a transition period between early and late stages of conserved gene expression which is characterized by phylum-specific activity of gene networks.
claims.source: A related term is 'mid-developmental transition' (MDT), referring to a transition period between early and late stages of conserved gene expression which is characterized by phylum-specific activity of gene networks (Kalinka et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kalinka et al., 2010.

claims.claim: The MDT phase, overlapping with the phylotypic period in previously studied animals, has been identified from sponges to chordates and may serve to define a phylum as a group of species that exhibit convergent gene expression during the MDT.
claims.source: This phase, overlapping with the phylotypic period in previously studied animals, has been identified from sponges to chordates and may therefore serve to define a phylum as a group of species that, during the MDT, exhibit gene expression which is convergent among themselves but divergent to other species (Levin et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Levin et al., 2016.

claims.claim: The conserved developmental mode proposed here applies to ESCs across phyla and entails the establishment of primary axial identity from an initially homogeneous or disorganized cell population, whereas the MDT and phylotypic period span the organogenesis phase of embryonic development.
claims.source: The conserved developmental mode that we propose here, on the other hand, applies to ESCs across phyla (albeit we acknowledge that this inference may be erroneous due to limited taxon coverage of existing minimal in vitro systems). Moreover, this mode entails the establishment of primary axial identity from an initially homogeneous or disorganized cell population, whereas the MDT and phylotypic period span the organogenesis phase of embryonic development, at which point the respective body axes are already specified.
claims.evidence: This is a comparative statement distinguishing the proposed conserved mode from the MDT/phylotypic period.

claims.claim: Future study of embryo-like systems may reveal further developmental modes, associated with the emergence of corresponding dynamical patterning modules.
claims.source: However, it can be conjectured that future study of embryo-like systems may reveal further developmental modes, associated with the emergence of corresponding dynamical patterning modules(Newman and Bhat, 2008; Newman, 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research, with supporting citations.

claims.claim: Additional developmental modes would not be universally conserved across the animal kingdom, but rather among phyla or lower taxonomic ranks, given that events following AP or OA axis specification often generate increasingly phylum or species-specific features.
claims.source: It is likely that these would not be universally conserved across the animal kingdom, but rather among phyla or lower taxonomic ranks, given that events following AP or OA axis specification often generate increasingly phylum or species-specific features of the larval or adult body plan.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference about the taxonomic scope of additional developmental modes.

claims.claim: Additional developmental modes could surface during the organogenesis stage of development and pertain to specific organ (primordia) specification or morphogenesis.
claims.source: Additional developmental modes could thus surface during the organogenesis stage of development and pertain to specific organ (primordia) specification or morphogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about when additional developmental modes might be observed.

claims.claim: Establishment of new in vitro embryo-like systems in conjunction with refinement of existing ones and investigation of their displayed initial patterning dynamics will help to assess if or to which degree conserved developmental modes exist.
claims.source: Taken together, establishment of new in vitro embryo-like systems in conjunction with refinement of existing ones and investigation of their displayed initial patterning dynamics will help to assess if or to which degree aforementioned conserved developmental modes exist.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the utility of future research.

claims.claim: Integration and comparison of studies on embryo-like systems with data from actual embryos should aid to more concisely delineate underlying mechanisms of primary axis and subsequent initial body plan specification in cell ensembles as well as to elucidate early embryo morphology diversification during evolution.
claims.source: Hence, integration and comparison of such studies with data from actual embryos should aid to more concisely delineate underlying mechanisms of primary axis and subsequent initial body plan specification in cell ensembles as well as to elucidate early (pre- and peri-gastrulation) embryo morphology diversification during evolution.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the expected outcomes of future research.

claims.claim: Figure 1 shows that metazoan embryos around gastrulation exhibit distinct morphologies but universally specify at least a primary body axis, demarcated by conserved expression of posterior (or oral in cnidarians) patterning determinants including T-box and Wnt genes.
claims.source: Metazoan embryos around the gastrulation or an equivalent developmental phase exhibit distinct morphologies and associated overall tissue rearrangement dynamics. Yet, during this event they universally specify at least a primary body axis, demarcated by conserved expression of posterior (or oral in cnidarians) patterning determinants. Among them are T-box and Wnt genes, localized transcriptional activity of which is highlighted in blue.
claims.evidence: This is a description of what Figure 1 shows, combining text and image information.

claims.claim: ESC or ESC-like populations from species across the animal kingdom can be (re-)aggregated in vitro and remain capable of recapitulating at least a basic transcriptional body plan with an anteroposterior (AP) and oral-aboral (OA) axis, respectively, despite lacking the respective external environment.
claims.source: Research efforts have shown that ESC or ESC-like populations from species across the animal kingdom can be (re-)aggregated in vitro and, although lacking the respective external environment and associated developmental cues, remain capable of recapitulating at least a basic transcriptional body plan with an anteroposterior (AP) and oral-aboral (OA) axis, respectively.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about ESC-derived systems, with reference to Figure 1.

claims.claim: Comparison of in vivo or ex vivo systems highlights a remarkable overall similarity despite the varying geometry of the respective native embryo, which may point toward the existence of a conserved developmental mode.
claims.source: Strikingly, comparison of examples of such in vivo or ex vivo systems highlights a remarkable overall similarity despite the varying geometry of the respective native embryo. This may point toward the existence of a conserved developmental mode that cells exhibit when released from their species-specific extraembryonic environment.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of systems, with reference to Figure 1.

results.result: Metazoan body plans are established during gastrulation through conserved gene networks and cell rearrangements, resulting in multilayered structures with one to three body axes that remain constant across phyla despite morphological diversity.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C5, C6, C7, and C10 collectively describe established knowledge about metazoan development and body plan organization. These claims are well-supported by the cited literature and represent consensus views in developmental biology.

results.result: Gene regulatory networks including Wnt/β-catenin signaling and T-box genes are evolutionarily conserved across species for primary axis patterning, though embryo geometry and tissue rearrangement dynamics vary substantially during axial emergence.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C9, C11, C23, and C24 are supported by multiple citations to peer-reviewed literature. The conservation of molecular mechanisms alongside morphological diversity is well-documented in evolutionary developmental biology.

results.result: Different metazoan phyla exhibit characteristic body axes: cnidarians and ctenophores have oral-aboral axes, sponges have antero-posterior or apical-basal axes, and bilaterians typically have three axes (AP, DV, ML) with bilateral symmetry.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C22 describe anatomical features of different phyla supported by multiple citations. These represent established comparative anatomy knowledge with appropriate literature support.

results.result: Bra/T transcription factor is a conserved marker of primary axis patterning that regulates morphogenetic movements during gastrulation, acts downstream of Wnt and TGF-β pathways, though T-box factors themselves predate multicellularity.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C33, C36, and C37 are well-supported by multiple citations describing Bra/T function across species. The evolutionary history and functional roles are documented in the cited literature.

results.result: Wnt signaling has been linked to the emergence of animal multicellularity as a facilitator of symmetry breaking and has not been identified in unicellular eukaryotes, plants, or fungi.
results.evaluation: Claims C34 and C35 are supported by citations to Loh et al., 2016 and Holstein, 2012. The phylogenetic distribution of Wnt signaling is well-documented.

results.result: Hydra and Nematostella re-aggregation experiments demonstrate that dissociated cells can reconstitute functional animals, with Nematostella requiring competent cell populations containing Wnt1/Wnt3-expressing organizer cells for successful reorganization.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C49 describe experimental results from cnidarian re-aggregation studies supported by appropriate citations (Wilson, 1911; Gierer and Meinhardt, 1972; Vogg et al., 2019; Kirillova et al., 2018). The data and interpretations are consistent with the cited sources.

results.result: Nematostella re-aggregates exhibit developmental plasticity with cells reprogramming their axial identity, employing alternative developmental modes (delamination, ingression, cavitation) distinct from normal embryogenesis but similar to other cnidarians like hydrozoans.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C55 describe specific experimental observations from Nematostella re-aggregation studies. These findings are supported by data from Kirillova et al., 2018 and represent documented developmental plasticity.

results.result: Amphibian and teleost explant systems demonstrate self-organizing capabilities, with dissociated cells from Xenopus and zebrafish able to undergo cell sorting, convergent extension, and axis formation, sometimes requiring external signals like Activin A, BMP, or Nodal.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C61 describe established explant experiments in amphibians and fish, supported by multiple citations (Ninomiya et al., 2004; Green and Smith, 1990; Green et al., 1992, 2004; Oppenheimer, 1936; Xu et al., 2014). These represent well-documented experimental systems.

results.result: Pescoids (zebrafish blastoderm explants) form polarized Bra/T domains, undergo elongation via Nodal and Wnt/PCP signaling, and specify all germ layers, though they require polarized inheritance of maternal factors.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C66 describe pescoid characteristics supported by citations to recent studies (Fulton et al., 2020; Schauer et al., 2020; Williams and Solnica-Krezel, 2020; Torres-Paz and Retaux, 2021; Zilova et al., 2021). The maternal factor requirement is explicitly documented.

results.result: Mouse and human gastruloids derived from ESCs mimic early embryonic events including elongation, germ layer formation, and axis patterning, with autonomous Wnt/Bra/T polarization initiating symmetry breaking and subsequent development of transcriptionally demarcated body axes.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C75 describe gastruloid characteristics supported by multiple citations (Doetschman et al., 1985; ten Berge et al., 2008; van den Brink et al., 2014; Beccari et al., 2018; Moris et al., 2020a). These represent well-characterized in vitro systems.

results.result: Human gastruloids (hGastruloids) generated from WNT-primed hESCs develop polarized BRA/T expression, elongate, and exhibit spatially organized expression of genes from all three germ layers, partly corresponding transcriptionally to CS9 human embryos but not fully recapitulating human-specific morphology.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C80 describe hGastruloid characteristics based on data from cited studies. The transcriptional correspondence and morphological limitations are appropriately qualified.

results.result: ESC-derived aggregates from Nematostella, zebrafish, Xenopus, mouse, and human develop oral/posterior Bra/T domains and exhibit morphological similarities (spherical then elongated), suggesting an evolutionarily conserved developmental mode that emerges when cells develop in minimal environments without species-specific external cues.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C87 present a major comparative inference across species. While individual observations are supported (C81-C84), the interpretation of a 'conserved developmental mode' (C85-C87) is speculative and based on limited taxonomic sampling. The authors acknowledge this limitation but the evidence is insufficient to definitively support the broad evolutionary claim.

results.result: mGastruloids specify endoderm and mesendoderm through alternative mechanisms compared to native embryos, initiated by mesenchymal-like primed ESCs rather than epithelial epiblast cells, though cells can be redirected to basal trajectories with appropriate factors.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C91 describe specific differences between gastruloid and embryo development supported by citations (Vianello and Lutolf, 2020; Hashmi et al., 2020; Anlas et al., 2021; Beccari et al., 2018). The observations are well-documented.

results.result: ETS embryos from mESCs and TSCs in Matrigel recapitulate mouse embryo development (E5.0-6.5) including lumenogenesis and cavity formation, with TSCs spatially confining Bra/T domain emergence at embryonic-extraembryonic boundaries, demonstrating the importance of extraembryonic tissues for providing signaling and geometric cues.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C95 describe ETS embryo characteristics supported by citations (Harrison et al., 2017; Arnold and Robertson, 2009; Langdon and Mullins, 2011; Christodoulou et al., 2019). The role of extraembryonic tissues is well-documented.

results.result: ETX embryos (mESCs, TSCs, XEN cells) mimic mouse morphogenesis until E7.0-7.5 and can initiate implantation responses but do not progress further; iETX embryos with induced endodermal cells better recapitulate anterior events including AVE migration.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C100 describe ETX and iETX embryo characteristics with appropriate citations (Sozen et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2019; Amadei et al., 2021). The developmental limitations are clearly stated.

results.result: Blastoids from ESCs and TSCs resemble E3.5 blastocysts with reciprocal cell type interactions; EPS-blastoids can develop post-implantation morphology with VE-like layers; human blastoids (hBlastoids) can be generated using similar approaches.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C108 describe various blastoid systems supported by multiple recent citations (Rivron et al., 2018; Sozen et al., 2019; Kime et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2021; Sozen et al., 2021; Fan et al., 2021). These represent well-characterized systems.

results.result: Various modifications to gastruloid culture conditions (matrigel, Wnt inhibition, growth factors, additional cell types) enable recapitulation of additional embryonic features including somites, cardiac structures, neural tissues, and gut-like structures in both mouse and human systems.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C121 describe methodological advances in gastruloid systems supported by multiple recent citations (van den Brink et al., 2020; Veenvliet et al., 2020; Rossi et al., 2021; Berenger-Currias et al., 2020; Girgin et al., 2021a,b; Xu et al., 2021; Olmsted and Paluh, 2021). These represent documented technical improvements.

results.result: Human amniotic-sac-like embryoids generated in microfluidic devices recapitulate post-implantation development including epiblast lumenogenesis, bipolar sac formation, and primitive streak specification before collapsing after 2-3 days.
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C125 describe amniotic-sac-like embryoid characteristics supported by citation to Zheng et al., 2019. The temporal dynamics and developmental features are clearly documented.

results.result: Comparison of in vitro/ex vivo systems suggests an underlying developmental morphospace with multiple trajectories; ESCs are developmentally biased by species-specific inputs, and alternative trajectories converge onto a conserved mode under minimal conditions but collapse toward native trajectories with external inputs.
results.evaluation: Claims C126-C128 and C133 present speculative inferences about developmental trajectories and morphospace. While individual observations are documented, the synthesis into a unified framework of 'conserved developmental mode' versus 'species-specific trajectories' is largely theoretical and requires more experimental validation across diverse taxa.

results.result: Blastoids and ETS/ETX embryos faithfully recapitulate early embryo morphology but cannot develop beyond E7.0-7.5, while gastruloids with abstracted morphogenesis reach E9.0 equivalent, suggesting that embryo-shaped systems are more constrained while pure ESC aggregates reveal greater self-organizational capabilities.
results.evaluation: Claims C129-C132 present an interesting comparative observation but the mechanistic explanation (C131-C132) is speculative. The hypothesis that embryo-shaped systems are 'more constrained' requires additional experimental support and may reflect technical limitations rather than fundamental principles.

results.result: The authors propose that embryo-like systems can reveal evolutionarily conserved developmental modes and inform understanding of body plan evolution, though more phylum coverage is needed and future studies comparing these systems with actual embryos will help delineate mechanisms of axis specification and morphological diversification.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C4, C14, C134, C135, C141, C150, and C151 represent the paper's central hypothesis and proposed research directions. While the proposal is reasonable and well-articulated, it remains largely speculative. The authors appropriately acknowledge limitations (limited taxon coverage, need for additional systems) but the core claim of 'evolutionarily conserved developmental modes' requires substantial additional evidence.

results.result: The authors hypothesize that evolutionary refinement of species-specific developmental modes and extraembryonic morphology ensures developmental robustness (canalization), with evidence from insect studies showing that oviposition environments drive egg morphology diversification and that extraembryonic structures influence gastrulation dynamics.
results.evaluation: Claims C136-C140 present an evolutionary hypothesis with some supporting evidence from insects (C137-C138). However, the authors explicitly state this 'remains unverified in metazoan embryos at large' (C136). The speculation about why some organisms are easier to generate from ESC-like cells (C140) is reasonable but untested.

results.result: The authors distinguish their proposed conserved developmental mode from the established developmental hourglass model and mid-developmental transition (MDT), noting that their mode applies to ESCs across phyla during primary axis establishment, while MDT/phylotypic period occurs during organogenesis after axes are specified.
results.evaluation: Claims C142-C146 appropriately contextualize the proposed conserved mode relative to established concepts (hourglass model, MDT) with proper citations (Duboule, 1994; Raff, 1996; Kalinka et al., 2010; Levin et al., 2016). The distinction is clearly articulated though the proposed mode itself remains to be fully validated.

results.result: The authors speculate that future studies may reveal additional developmental modes at the organogenesis stage that would be conserved among phyla or lower taxonomic ranks rather than universally across the animal kingdom.
results.evaluation: Claims C147-C149 present reasonable speculation about future discoveries with appropriate citations (Newman and Bhat, 2008; Newman, 2016). This is appropriately framed as conjecture rather than established fact.

results.result: Despite conserved Wnt and Bra/T roles, the diversity of embryo shapes and tissue dynamics points to a vast space of developmental trajectories accessible to embryonic cells, with topology shuffling in gene networks creating novel mechanisms; cells in embryonic contexts are constrained by embryonic and extraembryonic factors, while removing cells from native contexts allows study of inherent self-organizing capabilities.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C42 present well-supported observations about developmental diversity and the rationale for in vitro systems, with appropriate citations (Leptin, 2005; Solnica-Krezel and Sepich, 2012; Chen et al., 2013; Sheng and Foley, 2012; Christodoulou et al., 2019; Sogabe et al., 2019).

results.result: Figure 1 illustrates that metazoan embryos exhibit distinct morphologies but universally specify primary axes marked by T-box and Wnt genes, and that ESC-derived aggregates from diverse species can recapitulate basic body plans despite lacking external environments, suggesting a conserved developmental mode.
results.evaluation: Claims C152-C154 describe Figure 1 content combining text and visual information. The figure appropriately summarizes the comparative observations across species, though the interpretation of 'conserved developmental mode' remains the paper's central hypothesis requiring further validation.

results.result: Convergent evolution of anatomical features must be considered when evaluating molecular signatures; while direct correspondence between cnidarian mouth and bilaterian blastopore is accepted, substantial species-specific reorganization of mouth/anus formation occurs among bilaterians; the AP/OA axes likely represent the most evolutionarily ancient primary axes.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C28 present appropriate caveats about evolutionary interpretation with supporting citations (Martín-Durán et al., 2018, 2016). The inference about ancient axes (C28) is reasonable given available data though explicitly qualified as an assumption.

results.result: Annual killifish naturally undergo complete blastomere dispersion followed by re-aggregation, representing an in vivo example of multiple developmental trajectories as evidenced by differential anterior/posterior specification rates in embryos with/without diapause.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C68 describe natural killifish development supported by citations (Wourms, 1972; Pereiro et al., 2017; Podrabsky et al., 2010; Romney et al., 2018). This provides interesting in vivo support for developmental plasticity.

results.result: The authors theorize that stem cells from embryos prior to gastrula stage should harbor full developmental potential to self-organize body axes without external inputs.
results.evaluation: Claim C50 is explicitly speculative ('should, in theory') and represents an untested prediction based on the Nematostella experiments. This requires experimental validation.
